## Background

<!-- CHANGE THIS Write a few paragraphs about yourself here: where you came from before MUSA,
what drew you to urban spatial analytics, and what you're hoping to do with it. -->

📍 New England-born and previously NYC-based. 

👩🏻‍💻 I studied computer science and data science at *Worcester Polytechnic Institute*. I was also trained as a high school technology/engineering teacher through WPI's Teacher Preparation Program. I've worked as a software engineer for the past 3 years. 

⭐️ My interest in information accessibility and care for community outreach has manifested in various ways. I did undergraduate reserarch in learning science and educational technologies. I taught students technology, engineering, and computer science through programs like Girls Who Code and Engineering Ambassadors as well as in formal classrooms. I volunteer and am involved in outreach programs, both locally ([HYPER](https://hyperonline.org/) and nationally ([MITES](https://mites.mit.edu/)). I currently sit on the Alumni Advisory Council for Girls Who Code. 

🗺️ Through MUSA, I hope to bridge the intersection of data, computer science, and urban policy 
to enable positive change in underserved communities by broadening access to data that impacts them.
